recent_articles.title: India successfully test-fires Agni-1 ballistic missile from Odisha - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **India** successfully test-launched the short-range ballistic missile Agni-1 from the Integrated Test Range in Balasore, Odisha. The launch, conducted under the aegis of **Strategic Forces Command**, validated all operational and technical parameters of the missile system. This successful trial marks another milestone in maintaining India's armed forces' operational preparedness and strategic deterrence capability.

recent_articles.title: India battles power cuts as heatwave boosts electricity demand to record - World - DAWN.COM
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **India** is experiencing power cuts due to record-breaking heat and high electricity demand exceeding 270 gigawatts. **The government** has urged consumers to conserve energy, with outages lasting from 40 minutes to an hour in some areas like Chennai.  **Grid-India**, the national regulator, reported a peak deficit of 2.57 gigawatts late Thursday evening. Experts suggest that India needs to accelerate battery storage development to manage surplus solar energy during nighttime hours.

recent_articles.title: Lakshmi could have been a child bride - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Lakshmi**, a 16-year-old girl from Uttar Pradesh, wrote a song expressing her desire to continue her education and resist early marriage. Her father initially dismissed the message but was persuaded by **anganwadi workers** and **village pradhan**.  The village now features painted messages advocating for change in response to Lakshmi's powerful lyrics.

recent_articles.title: Congress workers clash with police in Jaipur during stir against NEET-UG paper leak - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Congress** party workers clashed with **police** in **Rajasthan** on Thursday during a protest against the NEET-UG exam paper leak.  Led by **State Congress president Govind Singh Dotasra**, the protesters demanded the resignation of **Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan** and the dissolution of the **National Testing Agency**. The demonstrators, carrying banners and placards, were forcibly dispersed using water cannons. Some protesters suffered minor injuries.

recent_articles.title: NEET paper leak row: Congress demands resignation of Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Congress** leaders demanded the resignation of **Dharmendra Pradhan**, the **Union Education Minister**, over the NEET-UG paper leak scandal.  They accused the government of a "money-making racket" involving people linked to the ruling establishment and claimed that the incident had caused immense trauma for 22 lakh students. **Rahul Gandhi** called for the Prime Minister's intervention, while **Mallikarjun Kharge**, the Congress president, alleged that the Modi government was undermining student credibility through repeated paper leaks.  **Jairam Ramesh**, a Congress general secretary, criticized the government's lack of action and incompetence in addressing exam reforms.

recent_articles.title: Medical Education Minister demands court-monitored probe into NEET paper leak - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Karnataka Medical Education Minister Sharan Prakash Patil** criticized the ongoing investigation into the NEET question paper leak, calling for a court-monitored probe. He expressed concerns that the **Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI)**'s current investigation lacked transparency and confidence, suggesting powerful individuals were involved in orchestrating the scandal to manipulate MBBS seat sales.

recent_articles.title: A reality check on govt.’s claim of 45 days of LPG ‘rolling stock’ - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **India's** government claims to have 45 days of LPG in stock, but experts question this figure given the country's limited storage capacity and reliance on imports.  The government has ordered several ships carrying LPG to arrive in India, with some already en route. The arrival of these tankers will contribute to the overall supply, although a significant shortfall remains.

recent_articles.title: NEET paper leak row: Youth Congress protests in Delhi, chief Uday Bhanu Chib detained - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **The Indian Youth Congress (IYC)** staged a protest in New Delhi demanding the resignation of **Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan** over alleged NEET-UG question paper leaks.  Protesters, including IYC president Uday Bhanu Chib, were detained by police as they marched towards **Pradhan's** residence. The examination was cancelled on May 3rd and a re-test is scheduled for June 21st. The IYC accused the BJP-led government of creating a corrupt system that favors wealthy students while disadvantaging those from poor backgrounds.

recent_articles.title: Mahanadi Coalfields gets govt nod for IPO; Coal India to dilute up to 25% stake - The Economic Times
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **DIPAM** and the **Ministry of Coal** have received approval from the Alternative Mechanism (AM) to allow **Coal India Limited** (CIL) to dilute its stake in **MCL**, a wholly owned subsidiary, through an offer for sale (OFS) as part of an initial public offering (IPO). The AM's approval also allows **MCL** to raise fresh capital through equity shares during the IPO and subsequent follow-on public offers (FPOs), qualified institutional placements (QIPs), or other Sebi-approved routes. The government stated that these disinvestment and fundraising exercises can occur simultaneously or separately, with a maximum dilution of up to 25% in **MCL**'s ownership by **CIL**.

recent_articles.title: NSUI holds protest outside Education Minister’s residence over NEET paper leak - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Members of the National Students’ Union of India (NSUI)** protested outside **Dharmendra Pradhan's** residence in Delhi, demanding his resignation following allegations of a paper leak in the NEET-UG 2026 examination. The protesters accused the Education Minister of failing to protect students and demanded a Supreme Court-monitored investigation into the incident, along with action against those involved. **The National Testing Agency (NTA)** cancelled the exam and announced it would be retaken at a later date.

recent_articles.title: Odisha CM reduces number of vehicles in his convoy by half - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Odisha Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi** has ordered a reduction of half the vehicles in his personal security convoy, following **Prime Minister Narendra Modi's** appeal for citizens to adopt cost-cutting measures due to global oil crisis.  Majhi also urged the public to minimize private vehicle use and prioritize public transport, advising against unnecessary travel and gold purchases.

recent_articles.title: School education index: Kerala betters grade, score - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: Despite the denial of funds by the **Union government**, **Kerala** has improved its performance in the **Union Ministry of Education’s Performance Grading Index 2.0 for States/Union Territories (UT) for the year 2024-25**. The state received a Prachesta-2 grade, an improvement from Prachesta-3 in 2023-24, with scores rising from 594.2 to 687.7.  **Kerala** achieved the topmost Utkarsh grade (72.8-80) in access and the Uttam-1 grade (81-90.9) in teacher education and training, among other achievements. The report highlights Kerala's progress despite challenges, including a lack of funding from the **Union government**.

recent_articles.title: Tata Power shares crash 7% after Q4. What are Goldman Sachs and Motilal Oswal saying? - The Economic Times
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Tata Power's** revenue for the March quarter declined 13% year-on-year to Rs 14,900 crore. However, EBITDA rose 10% to Rs 4,216 crore. The renewable energy segment contributed significantly to growth, with profit after tax before exceptional items rising 59% year-on-year.  Brokerage firms like Goldman Sachs and Motilal Oswal Financial Services maintain "Sell" and "Buy" ratings respectively on **Tata Power**, highlighting the company's strong long-term growth potential in rooftop solar and distribution, while acknowledging challenges with renewable energy generation execution.

recent_articles.title: Tata Power Q4 Results: Profit slips 4% YoY to Rs 996 cr, revenue falls 13% - The Economic Times
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Tata Power** reported a 13% year-on-year decline in revenue to Rs 14,900 crore for the March quarter but saw its EBITDA rise 10% to Rs 4,216 crore. The company's core businesses, including generation, transmission and distribution, and renewables, contributed significantly to earnings growth. **Tata Power** also reported its highest-ever annual PAT of Rs 5,118 crore for FY26, a 7% year-on-year increase.  The company attributed this success to operational efficiency improvements and growth across its core businesses, particularly in the renewables segment. **Praveer Sinha**, CEO and MD of **Tata Power**, emphasized the company's focus on long-term growth through clean energy expansion, transmission projects, and distribution improvements.

recent_articles.title: ECI set to roll out phase III of SIR in ‘coming days’ to cover 22 States, UTs - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Election Commission of India (ECI)** is set to begin phase three of its Special Intensive Revision (SIR) voter list process in the coming days, covering nearly 40 crore electors across 17 states and five UTs.  This follows completion of SIR in 10 states and three UTs previously, which has successfully removed over 60 lakh deceased voters from the rolls. The ECI had initially delayed the rollout due to Assembly elections in several states but is now proceeding with the revision process.  The exercise aims to ensure accurate voter lists for upcoming elections.

recent_articles.title: Education Budget will grow every year, says Telangana CM Revanth Reddy - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy** announced that the **Telangana government** will prioritize education, aiming for a 15% allocation in future budgets, gradually increasing from the current 7.6%.  He highlighted the implementation of several initiatives since December 2023, including teacher recruitment, DSC notifications, and global exchange programs. The "Exclusive Education Week" celebrations aim to showcase progress and improve learning facilities across the state. **Mr. Reddy** emphasized that education is an investment in the future and stressed the importance of teachers in building a better society.

recent_articles.title: Why a ministerial vacancy nearly delayed Class 12 Board exam results in T.N. - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **The School Education Department of Tamil Nadu** postponed the release date for Class 12 State Board exam results due to a lack of a Minister to authorize the announcement. This decision caused significant disappointment among students, teachers, and parents as it disrupted their preparation plans.  After facing backlash from various stakeholders, including child rights groups and educationists, the department reversed its decision and released the results on May 8th, as scheduled. Governor Rajendra Vishwanath Arlekar urged the department to release the scores without delay.

recent_articles.title: CITU calls South Coast Railway zone a “betrayal” of Andhra Pradesh, flags revenue loss - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **The Centre’s** notification operationalising the South Coast Railway (SCoR) zone from June 1, 2026, has drawn criticism from **the Centre of Indian Trade Unions (CITU)**.  **CITU** leaders argue that the new zone weakens Andhra Pradesh's interests by retaining key revenue-generating railway sections under the East Coast Railway (ECoR), and accuses the Union government of diverting railway revenue to Odisha. They also raised concerns over territorial jurisdiction, recruitment freezes, and privatization efforts, calling for a zone that serves the economic interests of Andhra Pradesh.

recent_articles.title: NHA recognises innovators for developing AI systems for healthcare claims processing and fraud detection - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **The National Health Authority (NHA)** concluded the Auto-Adjudication Hackathon Showcase 2026 at the Indian Institute of Science (IISc), Bengaluru, recognizing winning teams for AI-driven solutions to improve healthcare claims processing under the **Ayushman Bharat Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (AB PM-JAY).**  The hackathon, organized by **IndiaAI Mission** and IISc Bengaluru, saw over 3,500 registrations and more than 600 participants. Teams developed AI systems for clinical document classification, radiological image analysis, and forgery detection, with **Team Nirnaya** winning the top prize in the "Clinical Document Classification and Compliance to Standard Treatment Guidelines" category.  Winning teams received cash prizes ranging from ₹2 lakh to ₹5 lakh, and their solutions could be considered for future deployment within the AB PM-JAY ecosystem.

recent_articles.title: West Bengal Cabinet 2026: From Dilip Ghosh to Agnimitra Paul, Ministers who were sworn in along with Suvendu Adhikari - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Suvendu Adhikari**, newly sworn in as the Chief Minister of West Bengal, inducted five new ministers into his cabinet on Saturday. The swearing-in ceremony was attended by **Prime Minister Narendra Modi**, **Union Ministers Amit Shah, Rajnath Singh, J. P. Nadda, and Dharmendra Pradhan**, among other BJP leaders.  **Dilip Ghosh**, a senior BJP leader who secured victory in the Kharagpur seat, **Agnimitra Paul**, a fashion designer-turned-legislator who won Asansol Dakshin, **Ashok Kirtania**, a BJP stalwart who gained victory in Bangaon Uttar, and **Kshudiram Tudu**, a former school teacher from Ranibandh (ST) constituency, were among the newly appointed ministers.  **Nisith Pramanik**, a key face of BJP from North Bengal, was also inducted into the cabinet.

recent_articles.title: IPO Calendar: 2 issues to keep investors busy but mainboard activity remains muted - The Economic Times
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **RFBL Flexi Pack**, a Gujarat-based company that manufactures and trades printed multilayer flexible packaging materials, is raising Rs 35.33 crore through an IPO of 70.65 lakh shares. The company plans to use the proceeds for capital expenditure, working capital needs, and general corporate purposes.  **Goldline Pharmaceutical**, another company seeking to raise Rs 11.61 crore through a fresh issue of 27 lakh shares, operates an asset-light pharmaceutical marketing business selling medicines under its "Goldline" brand across various segments. The company plans to use most of the IPO proceeds toward repayment of borrowings.

recent_articles.title: NHA, IndiaAI Mission and IISc showcase human-centric AI solutions to transform health claims under AB PM-JAY - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **National Health Authority (NHA)** and its partners, **IndiaAI Mission** and the **Indian Institute of Science (IISc)**, hosted an auto-adjudication hackathon showcasing AI solutions for healthcare claims management under the **Ayushman Bharat Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (AB PM-JAY)**.  Teams presented AI systems capable of analyzing medical documents, interpreting radiological images, detecting document forgery, and streamlining claim processing. The event highlighted the use of AI/ML to improve the speed, accuracy, transparency, and efficiency of claims adjudication while reducing fraud and manual intervention.

recent_articles.title: Census enumerators ID can be verified through QR code - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Lalit Jain**, Director of Census Operations (DCO), **Haryana**, has introduced QR code-enabled identity cards for enumerators to address concerns about authenticity.  Jain explained that residents can verify the legitimacy of enumerators by scanning the codes on their ID cards. The first phase of the digital census, which began on April 1, aims to cover over 30 lakh households across India. Residents are legally obligated to answer Census-related questions, and while there have been no cases of FIRs for non-response, local authorities will be involved in encouraging participation.  The second phase of the census, focusing on caste enumeration, is scheduled for February 2027.

recent_articles.title: Telangana leads India in human trafficking cases, women form vast majority of victims - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Telangana** recorded the highest number of human trafficking cases in 2024, with 423 reported incidents, a significant increase from the previous year. This was followed by **Maharashtra**, **Odisha**, **Bihar**, and **Karnataka**.  The National Crime Records Bureau (NCRB) data revealed that sexual exploitation for prostitution was the primary motive behind trafficking in **Telangana**, accounting for 770 victims. The state also had the highest trafficking crime rate at 1.1 cases per lakh population, with a charge-sheeting rate of 99%.

recent_articles.title: Gurugram gated societies not letting in enumerators; FIRs recommended against enumerators obstructing Census work - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Haryana** administration has recommended an FIR against two government school staff for alleged negligence in Census-related work and obstruction of duties.  **Gurugram Municipal Corporation Joint Commissioner Punit Kumar** stated that enumerators have been denied entry into several highrise apartment buildings, prompting him to write to RWAs to ensure their access. **Registrar General of India Mritunjay Kumar Narayan** flagged off awareness vans across Delhi for the ongoing Census 2027 public outreach campaign.  The first phase of the Census began on April 1 and will conclude by September 30, involving around 30 lakh enumerators.

recent_articles.title: In a first, world’s smallest wild cat snapped with kitten in Faridabad; confirms breeding outside protected areas, say researchers - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Researchers**, including wildlife photographer Yatin Verma, have documented the first confirmed breeding of a rusty-spotted cat in the Delhi-National Capital Region (NCR) and Haryana.  The discovery was made during routine field surveys conducted since August 2022. The adult cat and its kitten were observed perched on a False Ashoka tree in Kot village, confirming active reproduction outside protected areas. This finding highlights the importance of the Aravalis mountain system for wildlife conservation, including the rusty-spotted cat, which is listed as 'Near Threatened' on the IUCN Red List.  The research paper documenting this discovery was published in Zoo’s Print.

recent_articles.title: SRF shares jump 5% as Q4 profit rises 11%; Rs 2,300 crore Odisha capex announced - The Economic Times
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **SRF**, a company based in India, reported strong financial results for the quarter ending March 2023.  The company's Profit After Tax (PAT) grew by 47% year-on-year to Rs 1,835 crore, driven by increased revenue and operating earnings. **SRF** also announced plans to invest Rs 2,300 crore in a new plant in Odisha, expanding its operations.  The company's consolidated revenue rose 7% year-on-year to Rs 4,615 crore.  Despite geopolitical uncertainty, the company remains optimistic about its growth trajectory.

recent_articles.title: BJP gears up to pick Bengal CM; Suvendu Adhikari front runner - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Amit Shah**, **Union Home Minister**, has been appointed as the central observer for the election of the leader of the Legislature Party in West Bengal, with **Odisha Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi** named co-observer. The BJP is set to form a government after winning 207 seats in the Assembly election, ending the Trinamool Congress's 15-year rule.  **Suvendu Adhikari**, who defeated **Mamata Banerjee** from Bhabanipur, is considered the frontrunner for the post of Chief Minister. The swearing-in ceremony is expected to take place on May 9th with Prime Minister **Narendra Modi** expected to attend.

recent_articles.title: Cabinet approves four more judges for Supreme Court - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Union Cabinet** approved an increase in the number of Supreme Court judges from 34 to 38, a move aimed at addressing the ongoing backlog of cases.  The amendment will be introduced in Parliament and requires approval from the **Parliament**. The current backlog stands at 92,385 cases, with several judges scheduled to retire this year. This decision follows a six-year hiatus since the last increase in 2019.

recent_articles.title: ​Lost and found: The Hindu Editorial on the 2026 Assembly elections - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The 2026 Assembly elections in Assam, West Bengal, Tamil Nadu, Kerala and Puducherry resulted in significant shifts in India's political landscape. The BJP secured victories in Assam and Puducherry while the Congress suffered its worst performance in Assam. In West Bengal, the BJP capitalized on long-term planning and a tainted election process to achieve a decisive victory.  The TVK led by actor C. Joseph Vijay made a historic debut in Tamil Nadu, becoming the first non-Dravidian Chief Minister. The Congress faces an internal challenge in Kerala with multiple candidates vying for the Chief Minister position. **Amit Shah**, Home Minister, is likely to gain further influence within the BJP as it continues its expansion across regions and social groups.  The results suggest a potential realignment of the Opposition, opening opportunities for the Congress to consolidate and galvanize support against the BJP.

recent_articles.title: West Bengal: Modi's BJP conquers one of India's toughest political frontiers
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) won a decisive victory in West Bengal, marking a significant breakthrough for **Narendra Modi** and his 12-year reign.  This unexpected outcome comes after years of the party's struggle to gain traction in the state, which has traditionally been dominated by the Trinamool Congress (TMC). The BJP's success is attributed to a combination of factors, including its aggressive welfare pitch, sharpened Hindu consolidation efforts, and a focus on alleged corruption within the TMC. This victory will likely have far-reaching implications for the BJP's future trajectory, potentially solidifying **Amit Shah**'s position as Modi's successor.
